The quick action buttons have no press action.
The greeting is always Good Morning.

terms.meaning: made-up sample values written into the code to show how a screen looks before real data is connected
moving the user from one screen to another
the address of a screen in the app

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the home screen
sections.what: Loads the layout pieces, icons, navigation tool, theme and shared UI parts used by the dashboard.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. These are needed to draw the dashboard.

sections.name: todayReminders
sections.title: Sample medicine schedule
sections.what: A fixed list of three made-up daily items: two medicines and one water reminder. Each has a time and a taken or pending status.
sections.why: Likely reason: placeholder data to show the design before real reminders are connected. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The Reminders tab reads real data from the server, so this list can disagree with it.

sections.name: recentDocs
sections.title: Sample recent documents
sections.what: A fixed list of two made-up reports, a blood test and a chest X-ray, each with a date and type.
sections.why: Likely reason: placeholder data for the design. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The dates are fixed in the file and will not update when real uploads arrive.

sections.name: quickActions
sections.title: Quick action definitions
sections.what: Lists the four quick action buttons with their labels, icons and colors: upload a report, scan a prescription, ask Maate AI, and share with a doctor.
sections.why: Defines the shortcuts shown in the grid. Reason for these four not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: This list only sets the look. The grid that draws these buttons has no press action.

sections.name: HomeScreen (part 1)
sections.title: Header and health score card
sections.what: Shows the greeting, the fixed name Priya, and a bell button that opens notifications with a small red dot. It also shows a health score card with fixed values for score, normal tests, adherence, water and reports.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The card gives the main summary at a glance.
sections.watch_out: Every number in this card is typed in by hand, so it never changes with real data. The score bar width is also fixed.

sections.name: HomeScreen (part 2)
sections.title: Quick action grid and today's schedule
sections.what: Draws the four quick action buttons in a two-column grid. Then it shows the Today's Schedule heading, a count of taken items, and the schedule rows with status icons.
sections.why: The count is worked out from the sample list, so it matches the fake data. Reason for the grid layout not stated.
sections.watch_out: The quick action buttons do nothing when tapped. View All opens the Reminders tab.

sections.name: HomeScreen (part 3)
sections.title: Recent documents list
sections.what: Shows a Recent Documents heading with a See All link to the documents screen. Then it draws one card for each sample document with its title, date and a type label.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. It gives a summary of recent uploads with a way into the full list.
sections.watch_out: The type label only replaces the first underscore with a space. A type with two underscores would keep a leftover underscore.

sections.name: HomeScreen (part 4)
sections.title: Document icon and text styles
sections.what: Sets the size, colors and spacing for the document icon, title and date.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. These are visual settings only.

summary: The main dashboard screen, showing a health score, today's medicine schedule, recent documents and quick action buttons.
purpose: Gives a quick overview on the first tab and offers links to notifications, reminders and documents.
why: The screen looks like a design mock-up. Most values are typed into the code rather than read from the server. Likely reason: a prototype screen. Reason not stated in the code.
how: Draws a header with a fixed greeting and name, a health score card with fixed numbers, a grid of four quick action buttons, a schedule built from a fixed list of reminders, and a list of two fixed documents. Some links open other screens.
inputs: Taps on the bell, View All and See All. Data comes from fixed lists in the file, not from the server.
outputs: A visual dashboard. Nothing is saved.
risks: Shows made-up health information, including a score of 82 and sample medicines. A real user could read these as their own status. The greeting always says Good Morning, whatever the time.
debug: If the numbers look wrong, check the fixed lists and score values at the top of the file. They do not come from the server. If a link does nothing, check the route names used in the navigation calls.
